content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
(1) Leveraging the latent cluster instead of classification can be used to alleviate the noisy labels sounds.
(2) The experimental results shows the promising performance of the proposed model.


Weakness:
(1): How to handle the situation when the visual difference is not significant between the foreground and background?
(2): How to determine the number of the cluster? Please give more details about the performance of the computation cost with different cluster.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a clustering-based foreground and background separation algorithm in assisting with the task of weakly-supervised temporal action localization. Particularly, the algorithm consists of two components: a snippet clustering component for dividing the snippets into multiple clusters, and a cluster classification component for classifying the clusters as foreground or background. In experiments, the proposed approach was evaluated on three publicly available benchmarks: THUMOS14, ActivityNet v1.2, and ActivityNet  v1.3.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 

- Proposes a clustering-based foreground and background separation algorithm in assisting with the task of weakly-supervised temporal action localization

- Develops an online self-training algorithm that optimizes the pseudo-labels and the model in an online fashion

Weaknesses

- Experiments/ablations seem lacking. According to Table 1, the proposed approach only improves over state-of-the-art approaches on THUMOS14 when using small IOU thresholds (e.g., 0.1:0.4) but not with large IOU thresholds (e.g., 0.5:0.7). It would be better to include detailed ablations and clarifications on the cases with large thresholds (i.e., strict metrics).

- The proposed clustering-based algorithm is complicated. It contains a set of indispensable modules (SCC, CCC, DDCL, TSCL, and CAT) and entails a set of hyperparameters (K^C et al) tuning. The performance improvement relative to the proposed complex algorithm seems a bit unjustified.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: An anonymous link to the implementation is included in the paper for reproducibility. But it contains a system consisting of a set of indispensable modules and entails a set of hyperparameters tuning.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper tackles the main problem of separating foreground and background frames in WTAL and builds on top of previous approaches, adding a clustering mechanism. There is a significant improvement over prior art on the standard THUMOS/ActivityNet1.2/ActivityNet1.3 benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- [S1] The biggest strength of this paper is the clear performance improvement on all the datasets.
- [S2] The idea of applying clustering to help with foreground/background separation makes sense.

Weaknesses
- [W1] This paper has too many components, making it hard to properly evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
- [W2] Ablation is only shown on THUMOS. This is somewhat related to [W1], as more ablation across benchmarks could better demonstrate the effectiveness of the clustering mechanism which is the main idea of the paper.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is quite comprehensive. The ideas are relatively clear and easy to follow, although it is not particularly novel, most of the ideas are drawn from other work. More ablation could improve the quality of the experiment section.
content.summary_of_the_review: My biggest point against this paper is the complex approach w.r.t its main idea making it seem a bit over-engineered. There is also a lack of ablation and experiments across datasets while the results on THUMOS is quite comprehensive. However the approach is sensible and the results are quite strong which in my opinion justifies the weak accept rating.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel clustering-based network named CASE for foreground and background (F&B) classification. It first groups the video snippets into multiple clusters (SCC) and enforces each cluster to be classified into foreground or background (CCC). In addition, the authors propose an online self-training algorithm to generate the pseudo-labels and a distribution-constrained labeling strategy to make them equally distributed across the clusters. The authors argue that the resulting cluster assignments can further refine the F&B separation. The proposed method shows good performance on three major datasets of the weakly-supervised temporal action localization (WTAL): THUMOS14, ActivityNet v1.2, and v1.3.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- The provided equations are comprehensive and also easy to follow.
- Experimental results are extensive where the ablation studies successfully justify the necessities of each proposed module.
- The proposed method outperforms all the previous approaches, which shows its effectiveness.
- Figure 1 illustrates the core idea of the proposed method very well.
- Figure 2 is also informative enough to explain which modules make up the proposed framework.

Weakness:
- Although the empirical results of this WTAL task are good, I am not convinced that the proposed method has a meaningful novelty that can contribute to the overall deep learning community. The main components of the proposed method are clustering and F&B separation. However, the authors propose a lot of different techniques (SCC, CCC, DCL, DDCL, TSCL, and CAT) to improve the performance, which makes it hard to analyze what the main contributions are and how they perform when compared to the previous approaches. I do not believe that each of the contributions is impactful enough.
- In this paper, a cluster is defined as a latent distribution of the snippet embeddings that embraces both the action class and F&B status. This means that the number of action classes can affect $K^C$ significantly. However, there is no analysis of the relationships between the action classes and $K^C$. Moreover, I strongly believe that a principled way of setting K^C is necessary, which is also missing in this paper.
- At this point, I wonder why $K^C=2$ is not enough to model the latent features when we only need to separate F&B. I believe that this is because the cluster-based feature separation needs an appropriate clustering method that heavily depends on data and task. Moreover, there are a lot of components in this paper, which probably makes it even harder to optimize $K^C$. Therefore, I think that the proposed method cannot be generalized easily to other data/tasks.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The authors do provide the code for reproducibility. However, the proposed method lacks novelty and has potential drawbacks stemming from the clustering-based approach. There are too many components that affect the final performance. The overall presentation is clear and the equations are easy to follow.
content.summary_of_the_review: I do not believe the proposed method can contribute to the overall deep-learning community in a meaningful way.

content.title: Clustering-Assisted Foreground and Background Separation for Weakly-supervised Temporal Action Localization
content.abstract: Weakly-supervised temporal action localization aims to localize action instances in videos with only video-level action labels. Existing methods mainly embrace a localization-by-classification pipeline that optimizes snippet-level prediction with a video classification loss. However, this formulation suffers from the discrepancy between classification and detection, resulting in the noisy foreground and background (F&B) snippets separation. To alleviate this problem, we propose to explore the underlying structure among the snippets by unsupervised snippet clustering, rather than heavily relying on the video classification loss. Specifically,  we propose a novel clustering-assisted F&B separation network dubbed CASE, which achieves F&B separation by two core components: a snippet clustering component that groups the snippets into multiple latent clusters and a cluster classification component that attempts to further classify the cluster as foreground or background. In the absence of ground-truth labels to train these two components, we propose to adopt an online self-training algorithm that allows online interaction of pseudo-label rectification and model training. More importantly, we propose a distribution-constrained labeling strategy that utilizes different priors to regularize the distribution of the pseudo-labels, so as to reinforce the quality of the pseudo-labels. With the aid of the online self-training algorithm and distribution-constrained labeling strategy, our method is able to exploit the latent clusters that are simultaneously typical to snippets and discriminative to F&B. Thereby, the cluster assignments of the snippets can be associated with their F&B labels to enable the F&B separation. The effectiveness of the proposed CASE is demonstrated by the experimental results on three publicly available benchmarks: THUMOS14, ActivityNet v1.2 and v1.3.
